annotations.text:
A version of Lilo I think is better — and the case for it.

This is a departure, not an extension. Last time you asked me to work inside Theme.swift; this time the brief was better, so I have argued with the structure instead of matching it. The three arguments are the deliverable. The screens on the next page are what they produce.

Read the arguments first. If you disagree with one, the screens that follow from it are wrong.

Five screens replace fourteen.

The trip is one page: countdown, who's in with real state, anything waiting on the group, the plan as days. No tabs. Add anything is one field that takes a pasted confirmation, a link or a sentence and proposes what it read — the parse preview is the whole point, since ParsedBooking already carries every field shown here.

Who's in is the screen Lilo does not have: a grid answering flights, room, bag for each person at a glance. The plan is days rather than categories, because that is how the week is actually experienced.

The dock is Partiful's — actions with the live count sitting in the middle of them.

Drawn with your assets and your photography. Sample content throughout: names, times, prices and references are invented.

Where this is riskiest

The composer only feels good if the parser is good. Yours is regex over stripped HTML and its own comment says "good enough for the user to confirm and edit". That is exactly right for a confirm-first flow — but it means the preview must always be editable and must never claim more confidence than it has.

One page also means one long scroll. If a trip grows to thirty saved places, sections need their own screens after all — but that is a rule about depth, not a reason to start with five tabs when a trip has nine items.
